To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 135C>C polymorphism of RAD51 gene, and Thr241Met polymorphisms of XRCC3 gene, as well as Arg188His polymorphisms of the XRCC1 gene are associated with colorectal cancer risk.
polymorphisms in the RAD51, XRRC3 and XRCC2 genes of the homologue recombination repair are associated with the risk of colorectum cancer.

the 135C/C, 135C/G and 135G/G genotypes of the RAD51, the 241T/T and 241T/M genotypes of the XRCC 3 and the 188A/A, 188A/H and 188H/H genotypes of the XRC2 gene are associated with an increased risk of CRC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect of the role of the homologus recombination repair in the development of colorectal cancer.
the identification of polymorphisms of the homologues recombination repair genes that may be useful for the prediction of colorectal cancer susceptibility.
the association between the RAD51, XRRC2 and XRCC2 polymorphisms and colorectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these polymorphisms are associated with the colorectal cancer risk, and the 135G > C polymorphism of the Rad51 gene can be used as an independent marker of the risk.
the RAD51 gene 135G>C, XRCC3 Thr241Met and XRCC2 Arg188His polymorphisms are associated with colorectal cancer risk in the Polish population.
the 135C allele of the RAD51 and the 241t allele of the XRCC 3 genes are associated with an increased risk of developing colorectal cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 135GC polymorphism of the RADS1 gene is a risk factor for colorectal cancer and the Thr241Met and Arg188His polymorphisms of the XRCC genes can modify this risk.
the 135GC polymorphism of the Rad51 gene, the 241TT polymorphism of the Xrcc3 gene and the 188HH polymorphism of the xrcc2 gene may be used as a biomarker of colorectal cancer susceptibility.
the 135C>C genotype of the RAD51, the 241MetMet genotype of the XRCC 3 gene and the His188His genotype of the XRRC2 gene may be associated with a decreased risk of colorectal carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 135 G>C polymorphism of RAD51, the 241Thr>Met of XRCC3 and the 188Arg>His of XRCC2 are associated with the risk of developing colorectal cancer.
the polymorphisms in the genes involved in the homologues recombination can modify the risk and the clinicopathological characteristics of colorectal cancer.
